task_name: Quill and Kiln - Autumn ceramics signature look
client_brief:
An autumn image library that still looks like my ceramics

Hi, I am Marlo Quill, the maker behind Quill and Kiln. I have a month's worth of photographs from my phone and a borrowed camera, taken under four different kinds of light. I need help turning them into a usable autumn collection.

Deliverables
1. Autumn studio journal carousel: 6 named exports. The image sequence tells a coherent making story. The captions match the pictured work.
2. Studio journal feature: 1 named export. The typography supports an editorial reading order. The feature identifies Quill and Kiln.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: A real person in a real studio
brand_identity.sector: An independent maker and lifestyle creator in Portland selling small-batch stoneware, with a seasonal coffee-bar collaboration each autumn.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Quill and Kiln, founded 2020, Portland, Oregon, a one-maker studio working from a shared space, with roughly nine thousand followers.
brand_identity.about: Marlo Quill makes small-batch stoneware in a shared Portland studio and sells it four times a year, plus a coffee-bar collaboration each autumn. About a third of what she sells comes straight off her own posts. The brand is the person: a real maker in a real room, warm and quiet, and never a polished label, because that is what her audience follows her for.
brand_identity.audience: Followers aged 22 to 34, the same age as Marlo, who buy 38 to 90 dollar stoneware and follow the maker rather than a brand.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A mid-tier creator retainer of 600 to 1,500 dollars a month, stoneware at 38 to 90 dollars. Above careless untreated phone photos, below gallery-ceramics gloss; a heavy uniform filter would read as selling out and cost her directly.
brand_identity.typography: Marlo Quill runs two families and four steps. Step 01, display and H1, is Erode Medium at 34 pt on 38 pt leading, tracked 0 units, which is also the wordmark's setting: quill over and kiln, lowercase, stacked on two lines, with a 0.75 pt Bench Ink rule the width of the longer line tucked directly beneath; carousel headlines take the same settings at 64 px on 70 px. Step 02, the subheading, is Erode Medium at 20 pt on 24 pt, tracked minus 5 units, and 30 px on 36 px in a carousel caption deck. Step 03, body, is Untitled Sans Regular at 10.5 pt on 15 pt, tracking 0, measure held to 65 characters. Step 04, fine print, is Untitled Sans at 8.5 pt on 12 pt, tracked plus 15 units, with piece names and prices switching to Untitled Sans 500 and tabular lining figures, 24 px on 30 px in a carousel. The name is never set in capitals and never letterspaced.
brand_identity.voice: First person, casual and direct. Example line: One look, mine, not a filter.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No formal brand files. Her three motifs, a mug, a sprig and a small kiln, exist only as ink on a photographed sketchbook page she keeps re-cropping. The true glaze colours are pinned by a single reference frame of fired test tiles rather than any spec, and there is no logo file.
brand_identity.values: One recognisable hand across the whole feed, with real rooms, true glaze colours and her own drawn marks.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The name is always lowercase and stacked on two lines, quill over and kiln, tracked at zero, with a 0.75 pt Bench Ink rule the width of the longer line tucked directly beneath it.

type_system.tagline: A real person in a real studio

scale.note: The stacked wordmark sets here: quill over and kiln, lowercase, tracked 0 units, with a 0.75 pt Bench Ink rule the width of the longer line tucked directly beneath. Carousel headlines take the same settings at 64 px on 70 px.
Carousel caption deck runs the same settings at 30 px on 36 px.

scale.sample: I make everything here in the shared studio, start to finish.
scale.note: Journal body measure held to 65 characters so the column stays one voice reading aloud.
Piece names and prices switch to Untitled Sans 500 with tabular lining figures so a price column lines up; carousel price sets 24 px on 30 px.

type_system.signature_move: The name is always lowercase and stacked on two lines, quill over and kiln, tracked at 0 units, with a 0.75 pt Bench Ink rule the width of the longer line tucked directly beneath it. That zero tracking and that rule carry into step 01, so the display row is the wordmark's own setting.
rules: Never set the name in capitals.
Never letterspace the name; the stacked wordmark stays tracked at 0 units.
The name is always lowercase and always stacked on two lines, quill over and kiln, never on one line.
The 0.75 pt Bench Ink rule is always the width of the longer line and sits directly beneath the stack.
The name and every headline set in Erode Medium; captions, piece names and prices set in Untitled Sans.
Prices set in Untitled Sans 500 with tabular lining figures.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
